authentication: none (anonymous calls work); optional free API key only raises the daily quota
cost_notes: free; no SLA and no commercial support; FDA may throttle or restrict access per its terms
entity_identifiers: applicant (submitter legal entity, free text; subsidiaries appear as separate strings)
openfda.registration_number (establishment registration numbers, many per record)
UNKNOWN - a UDI-DI is not on the 510(k) record itself; the link runs the other way via device/udi premarket_submissions
free_tier: free; no key needed (1,000 req/day per IP); free key raises it to 120,000/day
historical_coverage: 510(k) decisions from 1976 onwards; 176,529 records in the 2026-11-02 bulk export, 3,129 of them with a 2024 decision_date
known_limitations: no per-record first-publication timestamp exists: the source publishes decision_date and date_received only, so source_public_at can only be derived from the decision date and must be flagged as derived, never presented as a published-on date

`applicant` is the filed submitter entity; Medtronic Puerto Rico, Covidien, Philips Ultrasound LLC etc. are separate strings, so company linkage depends on the alias index and stays a candidate where the alias layer is unsure
`skip` is capped at 25,000: a complete backfill is only possible by splitting decision_date windows
the device model/UDI is absent, so 510(k) cannot be joined to GUDID from this side
openFDA is a secondary publication of FDA's CDRH database, not the legal record
licence: public domain: FDA dedicates openFDA content/data to the public domain under a Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal dedication (open.fda.gov/license/, verified)
rate_limits: documented: 240 requests/min and 1,000 requests/day per IP without a key; 240/min and 120,000/day with a free key (open.fda.gov/apis/authentication/, verified). `skip` is capped at 25,000, so full history requires splitting by decision_date windows
research_value: The densest free, machine-readable pre-market clearance stream for the US market, which is the home market of Medtronic, GE HealthCare and (for a large share of portfolio) Philips. decision_date gives a clean event clock for clearance timing and product_code gives the device-family join, so it anchors the US half of any cross-market device launch comparison.
timestamp_fields: date_received (filing date, earlier than the decision)
meta.last_updated (endpoint-level refresh stamp, NOT per-record publication)
update_frequency: continuous; endpoint `meta.last_updated` observed as 2026-10-26 for device/510k
